description: You are given two strings order and s. All the characters of order are unique and were sorted in some custom order previously. Permute the characters of s so that they match the order that order was sorted. Characters not in order can be placed anywhere.
intuition: Map each character to its position in the order string. Characters in the order come first (sorted by their order position), followed by characters not in the order string. Alternatively, count characters in s and rebuild by iterating through order first, then appending the rest.
approach: Count the characters in s. First append characters that appear in order (in order), then append remaining characters.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: order = "cba", s = "abcd"

Step 1: Count characters in s
  charCount = { a:1, b:1, c:1, d:1 }

Step 2: Process characters in order sequence "cba"
  ch="c": count=1, result=["c"], delete charCount["c"]
  ch="b": count=1, result=["c","b"], delete charCount["b"]
  ch="a": count=1, result=["c","b","a"], delete charCount["a"]
  charCount remaining: { d:1 }

Step 3: Append remaining characters
  ch="d": count=1, result=["c","b","a","d"]

Return "cbad"

Another example: order="cbafg", s="aaabbbccc"
  charCount = { a:3, b:3, c:3 }
  Process "c": push "ccc"
  Process "b": push "bbb"
  Process "a": push "aaa"
  Result: "cccbbbaaa"
explanation:
1. Count occurrences of each character in s.
2. Iterate through order: append each character count[c] times.
3. Remove processed characters from the count.
4. Append remaining characters (not in order) in any order.
timeComplexity: O(n + m) where n = len(s), m = len(order)
hints: Count characters in s, then place them in the order specified.
Characters in order go first, in the specified order.
Characters not in order can go anywhere (append at the end).
